name: Modal perfects: should have, needn't have, could have
subtitle: A modal + have + past participle looks back at the past. Use should have for criticism or regret (You should have called me), could have for a chance that was not taken (We could have won) and needn't have when something was done for no reason (You needn't have come).
source: icanspeak Spanish original English text (grammar-c1 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: You should have called me. — We could have taken the train. — You needn't have brought a gift.

qa.html: Looking back. We use modal + have + past participle to talk about the past and say what was right, possible or unnecessary. The modal gives your opinion. have shows that it is about the past: You should have called me. (You did not call, and that was wrong.)

Criticism and regret: should have, ought to have. You should have told me. (You did not tell me.) She ought to have apologised. With shouldn't have the person did it, and it was wrong: I shouldn't have said that. You can use it about yourself (regret) or about others (criticism).

A chance not taken: could have. We could have taken the train, but we drove. It was possible, but it did not happen. When it is said with feeling, it is a complaint: You could have told me! (You might have told me! is similar.) would have shows what you were ready to do: I would have helped, but I was away.

needn't have or didn't need to? You needn't have come. You came, but it was not necessary. You didn't need to come. usually means you did not come, or we do not say. Compare: I needn't have taken an umbrella (I took one; it stayed dry) and I didn't need to take an umbrella (so I left it at home).
qa.tag: needn't have or didn't need to?

qa.html: Two related patterns. was / were supposed to + verb: the plan or rule, often not followed: The train was supposed to arrive at nine. be bound to + verb: certain to happen: It's August, so the beach is bound to be crowded.
qa.tag: was supposed to, be bound to

qa.html: Typical mistakes: ✗ You should of called. → ✓ You should have called. · ✗ You should have came. → ✓ You should have come. (past participle) · ✗ You must have told me! for a complaint → ✓ You should have told me! (must have would mean: I am sure you told me.)

concept.noteHtml: Not a guess. She must have left and He can't have known are guesses about the past. See Modals of deduction. Here the modal gives advice, criticism or a missed chance. Spoken forms: should've, could've, would've, needn't have. Always write have, never of. US: needn't is rare in American English. People say didn't need to for both meanings. Basic modals are in Modal verbs. For would have in if-sentences see Third and mixed conditionals.

Meaning
Example

didn't need to + verb
rows: Yes, and it was a waste.
Usually no, or we do not say.
I {needn't have} taken a coat. (I took it.)
I {didn't need to} take a coat. (I left it at home.)

listen.text: You should have told me about the problem.
listen.note: should have + past participle: criticism. You did not tell me.
needn't have: you brought something, but it was not necessary.

listen.text: I could have won, but I made a silly mistake.
listen.note: could have: it was possible, but it did not happen.

hoeren.instruction: Listen and choose what you hear. Listen for should, could, would and needn't.

items.text: She could have been a singer.
He was supposed to call me.
They would have come if we had asked.

rounds.label: 1 · What was wrong: should have / shouldn't have
rounds.instruction: You hear what someone did or did not do. Say what was wrong with should have or shouldn't have.

example.prompt: Tom didn't wear a coat. It was cold.
example.answer: He should have worn a coat.

items.answer: She should have said thank you.
He shouldn't have shouted at his sister.
I should have locked the door.
He shouldn't have eaten all the cake.
We should have booked a table.

items.prompt: Mei sent the email to the wrong person.
items.answer: She shouldn't have sent the email to the wrong person.

rounds.label: 2 · It was a waste: needn't have
rounds.instruction: Someone did something, but it was not necessary. Say it with needn't have and the past participle.

example.prompt: I brought an umbrella, but it was sunny.
example.answer: I needn't have brought an umbrella.

items.prompt: We hurried, but the train was late.
Olga cooked for ten, but only four came.
items.answer: She needn't have cooked for ten.

items.prompt: I took a taxi, but the bus was just as fast.
items.answer: I needn't have taken a taxi.

items.prompt: Diego bought a ticket, but the museum was free.
items.answer: He needn't have bought a ticket.

items.prompt: They wrote a long email, but a call was enough.
items.answer: They needn't have written a long email.

items.prompt: You rang the doctor, but the cold went away on its own.
items.answer: You needn't have rung the doctor.

exercises.title: What does the sentence say?
exercises.hint: should have / shouldn't have = criticism or regret. could have = a chance that was not taken. needn't have = done, but not necessary.

exercises.title: should have, could have, would have or needn't have?
exercises.hint: Read the situation. What was wrong, possible, intended or unnecessary?

exercises.title: needn't have or didn't need to?
exercises.hint: Did the action happen? If yes (and it was a waste), use needn't have + past participle. If no, use didn't need to + verb.

exercises.title: What does the speaker mean?
exercises.hint: Tap the sentence, then its meaning.

exercises.title: Gap text: A trip that went wrong.
exercises.hint: Choose should have, shouldn't have, needn't have, would have, was supposed or were supposed. Read the sentence before and after the gap.
